----------------

🛠️ Tool
===================

Codync is a free, open-source client under Apache 2.0 that turns locally installed coding agents into persistent bots you can delegate to from a phone, desktop, or terminal. The README positions it as "the open-source Grok Bot alternative", using a bring-your-own-agent-and-subscription model with no paid tier. Everything below comes from the project README; I haven't tested the tool.

Key features:
• Agent coverage: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Pi, OpenCode, Grok Build, Gemini, Copilot, Hermes Agent, and roughly 40 more, each exposed as a messageable, persistent bot.
• Access surfaces: iPhone (iOS 18+, native App Store build), macOS 14+ (Apple Silicon and Intel DMG), Windows x64 installer, Linux AppImages for x86_64 and ARM64, plus any terminal.
• Distribution also available via Homebrew. The project ships a website, full docs, a comparison page and a Discord.

Technical implementation:
• The desktop host is written in Rust with an Electron front end.
• The iOS companion is built in SwiftUI.
• Agents keep running on your own machine, and model costs stay on your existing subscriptions; the app adds a chat-style remote layer on top.
• The README does not spell out how the phone-to-desktop channel authenticates or transports traffic.

Use cases:
• Dispatching a coding task to a specific agent while away from the workstation.
• Running several agents side by side from one interface instead of juggling terminal windows.
• Sending short follow-ups into an agent's existing session from a phone.

Installation, per the README: DMG for macOS (Apple Silicon plus Intel), x64 installer for Windows, AppImages for both Linux architectures, a Homebrew formula, and an App Store listing for iOS 18+.

Limitations:
• This is README-derived only; treat capability claims as unverified until tested.
• Bots inherit the local code-execution rights of the underlying agent, and the remote-channel security question above matters a lot on a dev machine. Review the architecture before pointing it at anything holding real credentials.
• Minimum OS requirements (iOS 18+, macOS 14+) exclude older devices.
• Per-agent behavior parity needs the project's comparison page, not the README.

One detail worth noting: the maintainers warn that @trycodync on X is their only official account, citing impersonators and scams around the project.

References: project site codync.dev, full documentation, and the GitHub repository leepokai/Codync.
